intro: Match each document to the world it was written in: when, where, and what led to it.

left.label: Hobbes, Leviathan, 1651
hints: 1651 is the earliest date here. What was England going through?
Hobbes wanted one strong ruler because he had watched his country fight itself.

left.label: Locke, Two Treatises of Government, 1690
hints: Locke wrote to justify something that had just happened in England.
Look for the choice about Parliament replacing a king.

left.label: Montesquieu, The Spirit of the Laws, 1748
hints: Montesquieu was French. Who ruled France in 1748?
He wanted power split up because in France one ruler held all of it.

left.label: Catherine the Great's instructions for Russia's laws, 1767
hints: Catherine ruled Russia. Who worked the land there?
Look for the choice that pairs the philosophes with serfs.

left.label: Wilberforce's speech to Parliament, 1789
hints: Wilberforce spoke in Britain's Parliament. What trade did he want to end?
Look for the choice about ships crossing the Atlantic.

left.label: Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, 1792
hints: Wollstonecraft wrote to a French lawmaker about who was left out of the new rights.

right.label: England in the middle of a civil war, when life without a strong ruler looked like chaos
England, the year after Parliament forced out one king and put another on the throne on its terms
France under an absolute king, who held the power to make, enforce and judge the law
Russia, where an absolute ruler who read the philosophes ruled over millions of serfs
Britain, whose ships still carried enslaved Africans across the Atlantic every year
Revolutionary France, writing new rules about rights that left women out

rationale.a: Hobbes wrote Leviathan during England's civil war. Watching his country fight itself convinced him people need one strong ruler.
rationale.b: Locke published in 1690, the year after England forced out one king and installed another on terms. He was writing to justify that.
rationale.c: Montesquieu lived under an absolute king in France. That's why he argued for splitting power so no one person holds all of it.
rationale.d: Catherine read Montesquieu and wrote about equal laws in 1767, while ruling a Russia where millions of serfs could be bought and sold with the land.
rationale.e: In 1789, British ships were still carrying enslaved Africans across the Atlantic. Wilberforce told Parliament he would never rest until that trade was abolished.
rationale.f: Wollstonecraft wrote to a member of the French National Assembly while revolutionary France wrote new rules about rights. Women were left out, and she called that tyranny.
